column4: Existing publication: Average-Case Integrality Gap for Non-Negative Principal Component Analysis — Afonso S. Bandeira, Dmitriy Kunisky, Alexander S. Wein. PMLR 145:153–171, official citation year 2022 (conference/PDF header 2021), Theorem 4; https://proceedings.mlr.press/v145/bandeira22a.html. Column C identifies the same work by its authenticated arXiv preprint DOI: arXiv:2012.02243v1, submitted December 3, 2020, Theorem 3; no PMLR-specific DOI is asserted. Full original unspiked Gaussian model with independent upper-entry variance 1/n: trace-one, positive-semidefinite, entrywise-nonnegative SDP value tends to 2 in probability and expectation; a proved true-optimum upper bound sqrt(2)+o(1) gives no rank-one SDP optimizer with high probability. Both original conjectures are refuted. Published and v1 PDFs visibly reverse the displayed GOE diagonal/off-diagonal variances. This is a mathematical diagnosis, not an author-confirmed erratum: the reconstruction explicitly uses invariant GOE, proves the exact diagonal transfer, and supplies the expectation argument; these extensions are not all quoted from Theorem 4. Original pages and the full core published proof were read. Sudakov–Fernique, Gaussian concentration and the global semicircle law are explicit imports with checked hypotheses. Montanari–Richard supplies the attributed stronger true-optimum limit; its AMP lower bound was not independently certified or needed. No planted threshold, practical finite-n cutoff, arbitrary non-Gaussian universality, unrelated hardness, novelty, or comprehensive priority claim. New exact diagnostics pass normal/-O/-OO with 17 controls per mode. This AI-assisted review is not a new publication or external peer review. PR: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/1314
